summary: Jellyfin is a self-hosted media server that indexes and streams audio, video, books, comics, and photos over a network. It processes media files for playback and provides client applications for various modern hardware platforms.
goodFor: Users who want to centralise their personal media collections and stream them across multiple devices without relying on third-party cloud services.
watchOut: Transcoding high-bitrate media files can demand significant CPU or GPU resources from your host server depending on the client compatibility.
deployNotes: You can typically run this software inside a container using Docker or via native deb packages, and you will usually need to mount persistent volumes for your media library and configuration data.
